skills.name: troubleshooting

39. #[verus_verify]
40. impl<T: Address> PageAligned<T> {
41.     /// Constructs a page address from an aligned virtual address.
42.     // Not-yet-verified dependencies (hal::mem trust boundary): the body checks
43.     // page alignment via `<T as Address>::is_aligned(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)`, where the
44.     // `Address` trait method is unspecced and `PAGE_ALIGNMENT` is an `arch`
45.     // `Alignment` enum constant the Verus front-end cannot translate. The body
46.     // therefore cannot be verified in place without speccing those upstream
47.     // `sys`/`arch` items (out of scope). `external_body` honors the `#[verus_spec]`
48.     // contract as a trust boundary, mirroring `FrameAddress::into_raw_value`. The
49.     // contract is the real caller guarantee; it is discharged when the `Address`
50.     // trait and the `Alignment` encoding are verified.
51.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
52.     #[verus_spec(result =>
53.         ensures
54.             // `from_address` validates; it never rounds/normalizes. On success the
55.             // wrapped address is unchanged (`result@ == spec_addr(&addr)`) and the
56.             // page-alignment invariant holds (`result.inv()`). On failure the input
57.             // was not page-aligned (value type: no side effect). Liveness is carried
58.             // by the `Err` arm: since `Result` is total, `Err => unaligned` is
59.             // equivalent to `aligned => Ok`.
60.             match result {
61.                 Ok(p) => p@ == spec_addr(&addr) && p.inv(),
62.                 Err(_) => spec_addr(&addr) % crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size() != 0,
63.             },
64.     )]
65.     pub fn from_address(addr: T) -> Result<Self, Error> {
66.         // Check if `addr` is not aligned to a page boundary.
67.         if !addr.is_aligned(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)? {
68.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, "unaligned virtual address"));
69.         }
70. 
71.         Ok(Self(addr))
72.     }
73. 
74.     pub fn into_inner(self) -> T {
75.         self.0
76.     }
77. }
